messages.subject: Re: rma background adjusted cel files
parts:
On Mar 14, 9:10 pm, "Karen Vranizan" <vrani...@berkeley.edu> wrote:
> Hi.
> I created rma background adjusted cel files as follows:
>
> > bgAdjustRma(cs)
>
> AffymetrixCelSet:
> Name: chip_data
> Tags:
> Path: bgRma/PilotExons/chip_data/HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core
> Chip type: HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core
> Number of arrays: 6
> Names: 1-con 1, 2-subcon1, ..., 6-subcon 3
> Time period: 2006-02-09 11:31:55 -- 2006-02-15 15:55:21
> Total file size: 376.99MB
> RAM: 0.01MB
> There were 12 warnings (use warnings() to see them)
>
>
>
> The bg adjusted cel files have a chip type header of HuEx-1_0-st-v1.1sq, like the original cels files. The path of the bg adjusted files refers to cdf type HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core.

Like quantile normalization, background corrected CEL files are
created by first copying the source CEL file and then update the
intensities. This is why you see that the CEL headers are identical
to the source CEL files.

You didn't tell us how you setup the AffymetrixCelSet 'cs', but the
last part of the path corresponding to the chip type is named
according to the chip type as returned by

cdf <- getCdf(cs)
chipType <- getChipType(cdf)

If you did follow Ken's example, I think you explicitly change the CDF
for 'cs' to the one for chip type HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core, correct?

>
> I'm confused about how to read these new cel files into a new AffymetrixCelSet. Could you explain that to me?

The path to the CEL files is bgRma/PilotExons/chip_data/HuEx-1_0-st-
v2,core/, you can always use:

csBg <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromFiles("bgRma/PilotExons/chip_data/
HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core/")

However, since bgAdjustRma() returns the background-corrected CEL set,
you can do:

csBg <- bgAdjustRma(cs)

I've updated the help pages a bit.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: rma background adjusted cel files
parts:
Hi,

try adding argument 'checkChipType=FALSE', which will turn of the
validation of chip type against directory name.

However, I recommend you to rerun the complete script, e.g.

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("PilotExons", chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core")
csBg <- bgAdjustRma(cs)
setAlias(csBg, getName(cs)) # See below

Since it detects if an array is already processed, it quickly skips to
the next one, so there is only little overhead in doing this and
you're sure you not grabbing another CEL set by mistake.

THOUGH, I just realized that you probably will run into problems with
this old-style bgAdjustRma() method; the name of the corrected array
set will most likely be "chip_data", i.e.

> getData(csBg)
[1] "chip_data"

A workaround for this is the setAlias() patch, which is why I added it above.

DETAILS: The reason for this is that the name of a data set is
inferred from the path, and as mentioned in several emails already,
bgAdjustRma() is a relic from early versions and should be replaced by
a new RmaBackgroundCorrection class. Ken, do you have time to update
this? [First step is to make sure it stores the output in probeData/
instead of bgRma/, *and* add tag 'RmaBC' or similar. Second step is to
create the RmaBackgroundCorrection class].

/H
